events.body:
C1: The driver cancelled on the rider's no-show claim without meeting the third NS-1 requirement: the GPS track shows the driver was within 200 m of the pickup point for only 2 min 30 s in total before cancelling (F2), which is under the required 3 minutes, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is not established and must be refunded in full. [F2 F4 F7] [NS-0 NS-1 NS-2]
C2: Even measured from the driver's own 'I'm Here' tap at 14:13:10, the system records only 1 min 40 s within 200 m after the tap (F6), so the driver's chat message 'Waited more than 3 min, cancelling' (F10) and his written statement that he 'waited for the rider' (F12) are contradicted by the GPS record, which wins over the driver's claim. [F6 F10 F12] [NS-1 NS-2]
C3: The stationarity facts confirm the wait was too short: the driver was stationary only from 14:12:50 to 14:14:50, i.e. 2 min 0 s, before cancelling at 14:14:50 (F3, F4) — 3 minutes of waiting was never reached, so none of NS-1 (i)–(iii) can be satisfied cumulatively. [F3 F4] [NS-1 NS-2]
C4: The rider's complaint that the driver 'cancelled after barely two minutes' is corroborated by the timeline (arrival recorded 14:12:20, cancellation 2 min 30 s later, F5) and by the driver's own message at 14:14 claiming he had already waited more than 3 minutes when the record shows he was 41 m away and had waited 1 min 10 s from his tap by that message's timestamp (F6, F9, F10). [F5 F9 F10 F6] [NS-1 NS-2]
C5: No exemption or alternative justification exists in the record: there are no traffic incidents and no speed-band records for the route during the trip window (F13, F14) and the weather was fair with no rain (F15), so there is no basis to treat the short wait as sufficient. [F13 F14 F15] [NS-1 NS-2]
C6: Because NS-1 is not satisfied on any element, NS-2 applies directly: the $6.61 fee charged on the record (F7, F4) must be refunded in full to the rider as a Ryde voucher. [F7 F4] [NS-2 NS-7]
C7: The chat record is complete with every message timestamped (F11), so the judge can determine the timing of the driver's 'I'm Here' claim against the GPS record without resorting to an 'undetermined' finding; the GPS facts (F2, F3, F6) control over the driver's written statement (F12). [F11 F12 F2 F6] [NS-1 NS-2]
C8: The driver's profile shows no prior upheld no-show disputes (F17), so no flag_account is sought against him; the rider's own clean record (F16, 0 upheld) is consistent with a genuine dispute rather than an attempt to avoid a legitimate fee. [F16 F17] [NS-2]
Weaknesses: The driver did tap 'I'm Here' at 14:13:10 while 39 m from the pickup point (F6), and his closest approach was 38 m (F1) — so NS-1 (i) and (ii) are arguably satisfied; the rider's case rests only on the third requirement, the >3 minutes of waiting, which the rider's side must show is not met. | The rider has not shown that the rider was at the pickup point at all; the driver may argue the rider simply failed to appear and that the 2 min 30 s within 200 m (F2) understates real waiting, but F2/F6 are system records and control over that argument. | The 200 m arrival radius is a data-layer parameter (policy gap G2), and the driver could argue he was 'at the pickup location' for longer than the GPS within-200 m measure suggests; the counter is that both the 200 m-based figure (F2) and the stationary-period figure (F3) are under 3 minutes. | The rider filed 1 dispute in 90 days (F16); while 0 were upheld, the other side may use the filing history to suggest a pattern, though RD/NS rules do not condition relief on filing history.

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.93)
events.body: This is a driver-cancelled no-show dispute, so it enters only through NS-0, which routes a driver cancellation claiming rider no-show to NS-1/NS-2 [F4][NS-0]. The trace settles the first two NS-1 elements in the driver's favour: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:13:10 (NS-1(i)) while 39 m from the pickup point, his closest approach being 38 m (NS-1(ii)) [F6][F1][NS-1]. The third element fails. After the 14:13:10 tap, GPS records only 1 min 40 s continuously inside the 200 m radius before the 14:14:50 cancellation, and the cumulative within-200 m time is 2 min 30 s [F6][F2][F3][F4][NS-1]. NS-1(iii) requires waiting at the pickup for more than 3 minutes (≥ 3:01); both the post-tap figure (1 min 40 s) and the total figure (2 min 30 s) fall short [F6][F2][F3][NS-1]. The driver's chat "Waited more than 3 min, cancelling" and his post-trip statement that he waited for the rider are party statements and cannot displace the GPS/timeline records [F10][F12][F6][F2][NS-1]. With any one of (i)(ii)(iii) unmet, the $6.61 cancellation fee is not established and NS-2 requires its full refund [F4][F7][NS-1][NS-2]. Quantum is fixed by the record: the only disputed item is the $6.61 cancellation fee, with surge 1.0× [F7][F8][F4][NS-7]; no formula computation beyond that figure is needed. The NS-2 supplementary flag is not triggered, because the tap was made while the driver was genuinely within the pickup radius (39 m), not outside it [F6][F1][NS-2]. NS-3's cancellation-rate flag is likewise not engaged: it concerns account-level cancellation rates, and the driver's profile shows no upheld disputes [F17][NS-3]. On the safety screen, the two chat messages are factual ("I'm here at the pickup point, grey Kia Niro"; "Waited more than 3 min, cancelling"), the complaint is about the fee, and there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation anywhere in the chat, statement or complaint, so SAFE-1 is not engaged [F9][F10][F12][F11][SAFE-1]. Nothing in the record is unsettled: the chat log is complete and fully timestamped, so no G12 gap arises [F11][NS-1].

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your cancellation fee dispute and we're refunding the full $6.61 to you as a Ryde voucher. The decision came down to the driver's wait time at the pickup point: the records show he was only there for about 1 minute 40 seconds after marking himself arrived, and 2 minutes 30 seconds in total — short of the more than 3 minutes required before a no-show cancellation fee can apply. The driver's account wasn't flagged, and nothing changes on your account. The voucher will be applied to your next Ryde trip.

DRIVER: We reviewed the no-show cancellation on this trip. The $6.61 cancellation fee was not upheld and has been refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher. The reason is timing: after you marked yourself arrived, the location records show about 1 minute 40 seconds at the pickup point, and 2 minutes 30 seconds in total — under the more than 3 minutes required before a no-show fee can be charged. There is no flag on your account and no change to your standing. Thanks for the detail you provided about waiting; it was noted.

what_would_change: Had NS-1 (iii) held ((iii) stayed at the pickup > 3 min after the tap, until cancelling), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled on the rider's no-show claim without meeting the third NS-1 requirement: the GPS track shows the driver was within 200 m of the pickup point for only 2 min 30 s in total before cancelling (F2), which is under the required 3 minutes, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is not established and must be refunded in full.

Even measured from the driver's own 'I'm Here' tap at 14:13:10, the system records only 1 min 40 s within 200 m after the tap (F6), so the driver's chat message 'Waited more than 3 min, cancelling' (F10) and his written statement that he 'waited for the rider' (F12) are contradicted by the GPS record, which wins over the driver's claim.

The stationarity facts confirm the wait was too short: the driver was stationary only from 14:12:50 to 14:14:50, i.e. 2 min 0 s, before cancelling at 14:14:50 (F3, F4) — 3 minutes of waiting was never reached, so none of NS-1 (i)–(iii) can be satisfied cumulatively.

The rider's complaint that the driver 'cancelled after barely two minutes' is corroborated by the timeline (arrival recorded 14:12:20, cancellation 2 min 30 s later, F5) and by the driver's own message at 14:14 claiming he had already waited more than 3 minutes when the record shows he was 41 m away and had waited 1 min 10 s from his tap by that message's timestamp (F6, F9, F10).

No exemption or alternative justification exists in the record: there are no traffic incidents and no speed-band records for the route during the trip window (F13, F14) and the weather was fair with no rain (F15), so there is no basis to treat the short wait as sufficient.
Because NS-1 is not satisfied on any element, NS-2 applies directly: the $6.61 fee charged on the record (F7, F4) must be refunded in full to the rider as a Ryde voucher.

The chat record is complete with every message timestamped (F11), so the judge can determine the timing of the driver's 'I'm Here' claim against the GPS record without resorting to an 'undetermined' finding; the GPS facts (F2, F3, F6) control over the driver's written statement (F12).

The driver's profile shows no prior upheld no-show disputes (F17), so no flag_account is sought against him; the rider's own clean record (F16, 0 upheld) is consistent with a genuine dispute rather than an attempt to avoid a legitimate fee.

weaknesses: The driver did tap 'I'm Here' at 14:13:10 while 39 m from the pickup point (F6), and his closest approach was 38 m (F1) — so NS-1 (i) and (ii) are arguably satisfied; the rider's case rests only on the third requirement, the >3 minutes of waiting, which the rider's side must show is not met.

The rider has not shown that the rider was at the pickup point at all; the driver may argue the rider simply failed to appear and that the 2 min 30 s within 200 m (F2) understates real waiting, but F2/F6 are system records and control over that argument.

The 200 m arrival radius is a data-layer parameter (policy gap G2), and the driver could argue he was 'at the pickup location' for longer than the GPS within-200 m measure suggests; the counter is that both the 200 m-based figure (F2) and the stationary-period figure (F3) are under 3 minutes.
The rider filed 1 dispute in 90 days (F16); while 0 were upheld, the other side may use the filing history to suggest a pattern, though RD/NS rules do not condition relief on filing history.

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint that the driver "cancelled after barely two minutes" is contradicted by the system timeline: the driver accepted at 14:09:00 and cancelled at 14:14:50, i.e. 5 min 50 s after acceptance, and the platform recorded the driver's arrival at 14:12:20.

Requirement (i) of the rider no-show test is satisfied: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:13:10, 39 m from the pickup point, and that tap is also reflected in the driver's own in-app message at 14:13 ("I'm here at the pickup point, grey Kia Niro").

Requirement (ii) is satisfied: GPS shows the driver first inside 200 m of the pickup at 14:12:20 and his closest approach was 38 m at 14:13:00, so he was at the pickup point both when he tapped "I'm Here" and throughout the wait.

Requirement (iii) is not met on the record, because GPS shows only 2 min 30 s cumulative within 200 m before cancellation and a stationary period of exactly 2 min 0 s (14:12:50–14:14:50) at 41 m from the pickup — at most 3 min 10 s from the arrival record; the fee therefore cannot be upheld on the current data.
The driver's belief that he had waited "more than 3 min" (chat at 14:14 and his written statement) is a party statement, and it cannot override the GPS/timeline measurement of the waiting time.

No aggravating account action is warranted: the driver has 571 trips in the last 90 days, a 4.58 rating, and 0 upheld disputes (route: 0, no-show: 0), so the abuse-of-button flag in NS-2 is not triggered and there is no NS-3 cancellation-rate concern.
The only money on record is the $6.61 cancellation fee with no surge (1.0x), so if the fee is found not to stand the exposure is quantifiable at exactly $6.61.

weaknesses: D4 is the crux and it cuts against the driver: F2 records only 2 min 30 s cumulative within 200 m before cancellation and F3 records a stationary period of exactly 2 min 0 s, both under the >3 minutes (≥3:01) required by NS-1(iii); the rider will cite F2, F3 and F5 to argue the $6.61 fee must be refunded under NS-2.

F6 shows the "I'm Here" tap at 14:13:10 while F1/F3 place the driver 39–41 m from the pickup; the rider can argue the wait clock started only at 14:13:10 (1 min 40 s before cancellation), making the shortfall even larger.

The driver's own chat (F10) and statement (F12) assert a >3-minute wait, but F2/F5 contradict them, and under the system-records-over-statements rule these assertions cannot be relied on — they may even read as an inflated claim rather than honest error.

points.response: Conceded on timing only, not on effect: F4/F5 do show 5 min 50 s from acceptance to cancellation, but NS-1 measures the wait at the pickup point, not time since acceptance, and F2 records only 2 min 30 s within 200 m — so the longer acceptance-to-cancel gap does not satisfy NS-1(iii).
Accepted: F6 shows the 'I'm Here' tap at 14:13:10, 39 m from the pickup, matching the driver's chat message at 14:13 (F9); NS-1(i) stands, but F6 itself limits the post-tap wait to 1 min 40 s.
Accepted as far as it goes: F2 and F1 support NS-1(ii), but those same facts record a cumulative within-200 m time of only 2 min 30 s before cancellation, which fails NS-1(iii).

This is the driver's own concession and it decides the case: NS-1 requires all three elements, so with the third element unmet the $6.61 fee does not stand and NS-2 requires a full refund of the $6.61 recorded in F7.
Agreed: F10 and F12 are party statements and lose to the system records in F2, F5 and F6, so the driver's asserted 'more than 3 min' wait cannot be relied on and the fee fails under NS-1/NS-2.

Agreed, and the rider seeks no account flag: F17 shows 0 upheld disputes and D6 correctly notes the F6 tap was made near the pickup (39 m), so the NS-2 abuse-of-button flag is not triggered and the remedy is limited to the refund.

Agreed on quantum: F7 and F8 fix the disputed item at $6.61 with no surge, so the revised outcome sought is a full refund of that exact amount under NS-2/NS-7, which both sides' records support as the maximum exposure.

Conceded on the arithmetic: F2 records only 2 min 30 s cumulative within 200 m and F3 a 2 min 0 s stationary stop, both under the >3 minutes (≥3:01) NS-1(iii) requires, so the $6.61 cannot be upheld and NS-2's refund_full follows.

Conceded: F6 shows the "I'm Here" tap at 14:13:10 and only 1 min 40 s within 200 m after it, so F10's "Waited more than 3 min" and F12's statement are party assertions that cannot beat the GPS record under the system-records-priority rule.
Conceded: F3's stationary period runs 14:12:50–14:14:50, exactly 2 min 0 s, and cancellation (F4) fell at the end of it, so no reading of the GPS data reaches three minutes of waiting.

Partly conceded: F5 confirms arrival was recorded at 14:12:20 and cancellation came 2 min 30 s later, so the rider's "barely two minutes" framing is closer to the record than the driver's "more than 3 min" claim (F10). I contest only the later part — nothing in F9 or F10 shows the rider attempted to reach or board the vehicle.

This point is irrelevant to the driver's outcome and I neither press nor resist it: F13–F15 describe route conditions, and the shortfall here is a waiting-time shortfall, so no traffic or weather exemption is being argued for or against.

Conceded on the outcome: with NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) not cumulatively met, NS-2 directs refund_full of the $6.61 charged on the record (F7), payable as a Ryde voucher under NS-7 — but note NS-2's additional flag is NOT triggered, since F6 shows the driver did press "I'm Here" at 39 m from the pickup, not outside it.

Accepted: F11 shows a complete, fully timestamped chat record, so there is no G12 evidence gap and the GPS facts (F2, F6) control over the post-trip statement (F12) — the timing is determinable and I do not seek an undetermined finding.

Accepted, and it cuts both ways: F17 shows 571 trips in 90 days, a 4.58 rating and 0 upheld disputes, so no flag_account is appropriate against the driver, and F16 shows the rider filed 1 dispute with 0 upheld — this was a timing error, not the abuse-of-button fraud NS-2 penalises.
